subject: OrthoGen dedicated capacity & isolation — post-call recap and next steps
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Jiang <sarah.jiang@orthogen.com>, Mike O'Neil <mike.oneil@orthogen.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-12T15:08:00-07:00
Subject: OrthoGen dedicated capacity & isolation — post-call recap and next steps

Sarah / Mike — thanks for the call earlier today. Quick recap here to make sure we’re aligned and to call out the immediate next steps.

Key takeaways (what you told us):
- Primary pain: production latency spikes and unpredictable token costs due to variable batch sizes across peak inference windows.
- Regulatory / isolation requirement: HIPAA-covered workloads; all PHI must be logically isolated and keys customer-controlled (KMS/HSM).
- Throughput target: ~150–250 inference QPS at steady state with 1–2x peaks. Typical request size ~300 tokens; long-tail contexts up to 2k tokens for specific study exports.
- Target latency SLO: p95 <= 150 ms for the primary model family.
- Desired procurement model: reserved/dedicated GPU pool (preference for committed capacity, with burst & autoscale to handle peaks).

Redwood recommendation (first pass):
- Start with a committed Dedicated pool equivalent to 8 A100-class GPUs (we’ll call this the "baseline").
- Configure autoscale to allow growth up to 16 GPUs during sustained demand spikes; implement burst fallback to hosted shared pool for short spikes, preserving data isolation for steady-state.
- Enable prefix/KV caching for common prompts and prediction reuse to reduce token spend.
- SLA: Redwood Dedicated standard SLA is 99.95% uptime; we can discuss a higher SLA with a multi-month committed spend.

Immediate next steps (owner / due):
- Markus: send draft SOW + pricing band for 8/12/16 GPU commit options (ETA EOD Friday). Attachment: redwood-dedicated-pricing-estimate.xlsx (draft).
- OrthoGen: share SOC2 / security questionnaire items you need evidence for (Sarah / Procurement).
- Schedule technical deep dive with OrthoGen infra (suggest two-hour session next week) — Alex to lead the runtime/ops portion.

Attachments included: orthogen-mvp-scope.pdf (scope & sample traffic profile), redwood-dedicated-pricing-estimate.xlsx (draft).

If that matches your read, I’ll turn the pricing draft into a short SOW and loop in Marissa to finalize commercial terms.

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com
(415) 555-0113

From: Sarah Jiang <sarah.jiang@orthogen.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Mike O'Neil <mike.oneil@orthogen.com>, Procurement <procurement@orthogen.com>
Date: 2026-07-12T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: OrthoGen dedicated capacity & isolation — post-call recap and next steps

Thanks Markus — helpful summary. A few clarifying questions and notes from my side:  

1) HIPAA / data controls — please confirm encryption at rest + in transit, and that customer KMS (AWS KMS / HSM) can be used for keys. We’ll need SOC2 artifacts for our security review. If you can send a short SOC2 statement or pointer, that would speed things up.

2) Isolation model — you mentioned burst to hosted shared pool: can you confirm whether any payloads or KV cache could be exposed across tenants during a burst? For compliance we need guaranteed logical separation for anything that touches PHI.

3) Pool sizing — procurement is inclined towards a 12-GPU committed option, with a 3-month evaluation (soak) period. Can you provide firm pricing for a 12-GPU commit and the terms for scaling to 16? Also important: what’s the minimum notice to increase committed capacity?

4) Trial / procurement timeline — Procurement is asking for a standard 60-day procurement window once the SOW is in place. Please include cancellation/early-termination terms in the SOW.

5) SOC2 / evidence — I can share our questionnaire, but please attach the SOC2 summary and any redacted evidence you can provide. I’ve CC’d Procurement who will coordinate the legal/SLA questions.

Quick ack: happy to schedule the technical deep dive. We prefer next Tuesday or Wednesday between 10–1 PT.

Thanks,
Sarah Jiang
Director, ML Systems — OrthoGen
sarah.jiang@orthogen.com

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Jiang <sarah.jiang@orthogen.com>, Mike O'Neil <mike.oneil@orthogen.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-13T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: OrthoGen dedicated capacity & isolation — post-call recap and next steps

Sarah — thanks, good questions. Answering inline and attaching requested docs.

1) Encryption / KMS: Confirmed — Redwood Dedicated supports customer-managed keys (AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS, or on-prem HSM). All storage and snapshots are encrypted at rest. In transit uses TLS 1.2+. Attaching: SOC2-summary.pdf.

2) Isolation & burst behavior: When a request is routed to a Redwood-hosted shared pool for short bursts, we do not write OrthoGen KV caches to the shared tenant space. For PHI workloads we recommend enabling a reserved pool for any production requests that touch PHI; burst to shared pool is suitable for stateless, non-PHI inference. We’ll include an isolation appendix in the SOW that codifies no cross-tenant KV sharing and data-handling rules.

3) Pool sizing & pricing: Based on your traffic profile, recommended path: start with 8 GPUs baseline, commit to 12 GPUs if procurement prefers a middle ground, with autoscale to 16 for sustained spikes. Marissa — can you confirm the committed pricing for 8/12/16 options and a pro-rata cancellation schedule? Also include a line for optional 99.98% SLA uplift (price delta). See attached pricing spreadsheet for ranges; I’ll turn these into a formal SOW once we confirm the target commit.

4) Notice to scale committed capacity: We can accept scale increases with 14 days’ notice for committed capacity. For immediate bursts we use shared capacity with billing adjustments. We’ll call out notice periods in the SOW.

5) Procurement / SOW: I’ll draft the SOW and include the 60-day procurement window language and termination terms. Tentative schedule: SOW draft by EOD Friday; technical deep-dive Tue/Wed next week (Alex to propose meeting time).

Related links: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/6789012/OG-2026-137 (deal record); https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cOrthoGen-Discovery (shared discovery folder).

Attachments: SOC2-summary.pdf, SOC2-evidence-request.xlsx (template).

Markus
